definitions: A tradition within the Anglican Church that emphasizes the Protestant nature of Anglicanism, the importance of personal conversion, and the authority of the Bible, often with simpler liturgy and less emphasis on ritual and sacraments.
A group of people or a church adhering to the low church tradition.
examples: Many evangelicals identify with the low church.
The low church often prefers simpler vestments.
Historically, the low church has been influential in missionary work.
